context.full_target: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1 with Chevalley generators x,y,h, every nonzero v∈V with xv=0 and hv=λv, and every arbitrary admissible lattice M⊂V (a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all x^r/r!,y^r/r!), prove that V(K)=M⊗ℤK is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V(K). Here L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗ℤK acts by the induced lattice operators, including the Chevalley construction in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure assumption on K is made, and λ=0 and p=2 are included.
context.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, including λ=0 and p=2, over the given arbitrary field K.

record.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by nonnegative integers

record.definition: U_Z is the ℤ-subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers x^r/r!,y^r/r! for integers r≥0; their actions on V are X_r,Y_r.

record.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p does not divide b}, with the usual rational arithmetic and its embedding into ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Once its multiplication map into V is proved injective, it is identified with its image in V.
ι_R is the tensor multiplication map determined by ι_R(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R and m∈M, using the rational scalar action on V.

record.definition: For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k∈I and k≠j to zero. This definition is made only after (e_k)_{k∈I} has been proved to be a complex basis of V.

record.definition: V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K. Every ℤ-linear operator on M acts by its tensor extension on V(K). The same symbols x,y,h,X_r,Y_r denote the tensor-induced actions of their restrictions to M once their preservation of M has been proved; this notation asserts no such preservation by itself.

L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, the scalar extension of the Chevalley ℤ-form with the commutator bracket inherited from sl₂(C). This is the Chevalley sl₂ construction also when the characteristic is 2. Its action on V(K) is induced from the actions on M.

record.statement: n=λ+1>0 and card(I)=n. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V; e_0=v. For every integer m≥0, h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v; for m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v. The vectors y^m v vanish for m>λ. The action matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix coefficients are integers.

record.statement: ι_R:M_R→V is injective, its image spans V over ℂ, and M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, of rank n. Every X_r,Y_r (r≥0) preserves M and, under this embedding, also preserves M_R. For every integer t with 0≤t≤λ, t! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M and give its induced Chevalley action after tensoring.
record.origin: problem.md:86-116; basis and tensor identification made explicit.

record.statement: n>0. All the R-submodules Jcoord_i (i∈I) equal J. J is nonzero and finitely generated over R. Inside V one has M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i: explicitly every element of M_R has a unique expression ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i with c_i∈J, and every such finite sum belongs to M_R. Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map T→ℂ, q⊗c↦qc, is injective, T is finite dimensional over ℚ and dim_ℚ T=1. For every nonzero a∈J and every c∈J there exists q∈ℚ with c=qa.
record.origin: problem.md:118-140, including the essential rank-one argument rather than inferring rank from containment in ℂ.

record.statement: There exists b∈J with b≠0 such that J=Rb. For any such b, the vectors (b e_i)_{i∈I} form an R-basis of M_R (identified with its image under ι_R), of cardinality n>0.

The integer map ℤ→K extends to ρ:R→K, ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms V(K)=M⊗_ℤK ≃ M_R⊗_R K ≃ (M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K, where ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ acts on K by the prime-field embedding. V(K) has a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of cardinality n>0, obtained from b e_i for a nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, and hence dim_K V(K)=n. The operators x,y,h and X_r,Y_r here are the tensor-induced lattice operators. The actions of x,y,h give the induced representation of the Chevalley ℤ-form tensored with K, and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h on V(K). On β they and all the divided powers have the following integer matrices reduced to K: xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ; yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i; X_rβ_i=bar(binom(λ-i+r,r))β_{i-r} for r≤i and zero otherwise, Y_rβ_i=bar(binom(i+r,r))β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. For 0≤r≤λ, bar(r!)≠0, X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r. For all i,j∈I the K-linear coordinate matrix unit T_ij relative to β is bar(binom(λ,j))^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Consequently every K-linear subspace of V(K) invariant under x,y is invariant under every T_ij.
